lede.headline: AI chip stocks sink in broad Thursday selloff
lede.dek: AMD and Marvell each fell about 8% on Oct. 22 after a supply-chain warning from Lam Research and a jump in oil prices rattled investors in AI-linked chipmakers.

top10AsOf: List as of Sep 24, 2026 9:15 PM ET

stories.headline: AMD stock drops 8% as chip-sector selloff deepens
stories.move: AMD shares fell 8.1% to $507.93 on Oct. 22, part of a broader tech selloff after chipmaking-equipment supplier Lam Research warned on Oct. 21 that supply-chain constraints were limiting its own revenue guidance, and as oil prices jumped on renewed Middle East conflict.
stories.why: The drop shows how exposed AI-chip stocks are to supply-chain and macro shocks even when the companies' own results are strong.
stories.bear: AMD's business hasn't changed; one bad trading day in a volatile sector doesn't reflect the company's actual AI chip demand.
stories.watch: AMD's next earnings report, expected in early November 2026.

stories.headline: Marvell falls 8% in broad AI chip selloff
stories.move: Marvell shares fell about 8% on Oct. 22 to $224.64 in morning trading, part of a semiconductor-wide selloff triggered by chipmaking-equipment supplier Lam Research, which warned on Oct. 21 that supply constraints were limiting its own revenue guidance.
stories.why: The selloff hit a stock Charles Koch's family holds as an investment, underscoring how sensitive AI-chip investors remain to supply-chain warnings.
stories.bear: Marvell had already rallied sharply this year; some of the drop looks like profit-taking after a steep run-up rather than a change in its own business.
stories.watch: Whether other chip-equipment makers confirm or ease Lam Research's supply warning in their own results.

stories.headline: Kering stock sinks 12% as Gucci sales keep falling
stories.move: Kering reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of 3.35 billion euros on Oct. 22, roughly flat and in line with estimates, but sales at its largest brand, Gucci, fell 6% on a comparable basis, with Gucci's retail sales down 9%; shares slid in early trading as investors weighed the cost and pace of the Gucci turnaround.
stories.why: Gucci drives most of Kering's profit, so another quarter of weak sales there raises doubts about the pace of the turnaround Pinault's family is counting on.
stories.bear: Kering's jewelry and eyewear divisions grew strongly, so the group isn't shrinking everywhere, and management said October trends were in line with the quarter.
stories.watch: Kering's full-year 2026 results and any update on Gucci's turnaround plan.

stories.headline: Blackstone shares jump 8% on strong third-quarter results
stories.move: Blackstone shares rose about 8.4% on Oct. 22 after the firm reported third-quarter distributable earnings of $1.7 billion, or $1.32 a share, above the $1.29 analysts expected, with total assets under management reaching a record $1.4 trillion, up 10% from a year earlier.
stories.why: The jump shows investors rewarding Blackstone's fee income and profitability even as some rivals in private markets face slower dealmaking.
stories.bear: Revenue of $3.06 billion came in below the $3.35 billion analysts expected, so not every part of the quarter beat forecasts.
stories.watch: Blackstone's next dividend payment, declared at $1.12 a share for holders of record on Nov. 2, 2026.

stories.headline: Spotify shares jump as revenue and users top expectations
stories.move: Spotify reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of 5.0 billion euros, up 16% year over year, with premium subscribers growing 9% to 306 million and monthly active users up 11% to 788 million; the company said gross margin and operating income came in ahead of its own guidance.
stories.why: Strong subscriber and profit growth support Daniel Ek's push to make Spotify consistently profitable, not just bigger.
stories.bear: GAAP diluted earnings per share came in below the consensus estimate, ending a run of quarterly beats, which some investors read as a yellow flag.
stories.watch: Spotify's fourth-quarter operating income guidance of about 820 million euros.

stories.headline: SoftBank shares fall as AI debt worries deepen
stories.move: SoftBank Group shares fell 6.9% in Tokyo on Oct. 22 to close at 4,305 yen, about half their record closing price from June, as rising borrowing costs raised doubts about the sustainability of Masayoshi Son's heavy AI investment spending.
stories.why: The decline reflects growing investor concern about how SoftBank will keep funding its enormous bets on OpenAI and other AI companies as borrowing costs climb.
stories.bear: SoftBank's underlying AI stakes, including in OpenAI, haven't been written down; the drop is about financing worries, not a confirmed loss in value.
stories.watch: SoftBank's next earnings report, due Nov. 10, 2026, for an update on its OpenAI funding commitments.

stories.headline: Tesla beats on profit and deliveries, but revenue is flat
stories.move: Tesla reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $28.05 billion, flat from a year earlier, with non-GAAP earnings per share of $0.48 beating the $0.45 consensus though down 4% from a year ago; the company delivered 486,532 vehicles, above the 461,974 analysts expected but down 2.1% year over year.
stories.why: The quarter shows Tesla stabilizing profit margins even as vehicle deliveries keep shrinking from a year ago, a trend Elon Musk has leaned on robotaxi and energy-storage growth to offset.
stories.bear: Energy storage deployments of 13.7 GWh missed the roughly 15.9 GWh analysts expected, showing growth has slowed in the business Tesla has pointed to as its next driver.
stories.watch: Tesla's full fourth-quarter delivery and production numbers, typically reported in early January.

stories.headline: Eric Schmidt's early Anthropic bet nears a huge payout
stories.move: Bloomberg reported on Oct. 19 that former Google CEO Eric Schmidt owns roughly 1% of Anthropic, a stake built by investing in the AI company's 2021 Series A round; Reuters reported the week before that some investors have discussed an IPO valuation around $1.5 trillion, down from earlier talk of about $2 trillion.
stories.why: If Anthropic goes public near those valuations, Schmidt's stake could be worth billions, making him one of the AI boom's biggest individual winners outside the companies he has run.
stories.bear: The valuation range is still being debated by investors and could move again before any IPO actually prices, and the exact size of Schmidt's stake hasn't been confirmed.
stories.watch: Anthropic's IPO marketing, which could begin as early as Nov. 9, 2026.

stories.headline: Dangote refinery extends IPO deadline on strong demand
stories.move: Dangote Petroleum Refinery extended the application deadline for its roughly $1.6 billion initial public offering by two weeks, to Oct. 27, after Nigeria's securities regulator approved the change; the company cited strong investor demand across Africa and said the extra time would let more applicants finish account-opening and identity checks.
stories.why: A well-subscribed offering would mark one of Africa's largest IPOs and give Aliko Dangote's refinery a much broader shareholder base beyond his own holding.
stories.bear: A longer subscription window can also signal the offer wasn't filling fast enough by the original deadline, not just rising demand.
stories.watch: The new Oct. 27 deadline and the planned share-allotment announcement to Nigeria's SEC on Nov. 10, 2026.

watch: Oct. 27, 2026: Dangote refinery's extended IPO subscription deadline closes.
Nov. 9, 2026: Anthropic's IPO marketing could begin, per reports.
Nov. 10, 2026: Dangote refinery's planned share-allotment announcement to Nigeria's SEC.
quickHits: Intel shares fell about 7% in the same Oct. 22 chip-sector selloff tied to Lam Research's supply-chain warning that hit AMD and Marvell.
Oil prices topped $112 a barrel on Oct. 22 after renewed attacks in Saudi Arabia, adding to the pressure on AI-chip stocks that day.
memo: A single supplier's cautious guidance (Lam Research) can swing an entire sector's stock prices in a day; know how exposed your own business is to one supplier's outlook.
Even strong operating results (Spotify, Blackstone) can be overshadowed by one weak line item; know which numbers your own investors or lenders watch most closely.
Rising borrowing costs are starting to squeeze even well-capitalized companies with aggressive growth bets (SoftBank); rising rates change the math on big, debt-funded expansion plans.

movers.why: Kering fell 12.2% after Gucci's third-quarter sales dropped 6%, even as total group revenue matched estimates.
Spotify rose 11.1% after the company reported third-quarter revenue grew 16% and profit topped expectations.
Marvell fell 8.7% after chip-equipment maker Lam Research warned of supply constraints, hitting semiconductor stocks.
Blackstone rose 8.4% after third-quarter results showed record fee income and strong profit margins.
SoftBank fell 8.2% after reports said rising borrowing costs raised doubts about its heavy AI spending.
AMD fell 8.1% after oil prices jumped on renewed Middle East conflict, adding to worries about AI spending costs.
